messages:
maya: FYI onboarding vectora-9b-ptq-v1 post-canary, seeing odd currency conversion answers + latency on larger batches. sample outputs below.
riya: can you paste a reproducer and which quant config you used?
maya: running PTQ 4-bit symmetric on A100, config: 
```json
{"quant_bits":4, "scheme":"sym", "per_channel":true, "clip_threshold":0.0}
```
maya: example prompt -> "Convert $100 to EUR at 2024-03-01 rate"
maya: vectora-9b-ptq-v1 answer -> "€11,400" (obviously wrong)
maya: fp16 baseline answer -> "€92.00"
axel: tagging infra for kernel/driver check @axel
axel: I didn't push any runtime changes since yesterday; we did update CUDA 12.2 driver on canary hosts last night — I'll diff kernel selection and driver logs.
sam: latency numbers? what's the batch size and seq length for repro?
maya: batch=8, avg seq=128; p50 went from ~210ms -> ~480ms after rollout; p95 ~1.2s. Repro script: 
```bash
python -m eval_run --model vectora-9b-ptq-v1 --batch 8 --seq 128 --num 50
```
riya: interesting — PTQ can make logits more peaky or shift offsets. do we have logits histograms pre/post quant?
maya: attaching small snippet in the eval logs: mean/std changed, topk mass concentrated on fewer tokens.
maya: also seeing nonsense numeric scale on currencies and occasionally dates (e.g., returns year 2109).
nora: mitigation: route traffic to fallback fp16 variant and consider rollback if SLAs or quality impacted for customers.
deploy-bot: deploy started: rolling back vectora-9b-ptq-v1 -> vectora-9b-fp16-v1, rollouts in progress :hourglass:
axel: infra will revert CUDA on one canary host and run microbenchmarks to confirm driver impact.
sam: check fused-attn path — PTQ kernel selection might choose a slower/unfused codepath at certain seq lengths which explains latency spike. also check memcpy patterns.
riya: plan of attack: 1) run eval harness full suite for money/date conversions vs fp16 baseline; 2) repro with deterministic sampling (topk=1, temp=0.0) to separate sampling from logits calibration issues; 3) test qconfigs: per-channel vs per-tensor and asymmetric clipping thresholds; 4) verify KV cache token alignment and eos mapping.
maya: started eval run id run_20260320_01, uploading logs to s3://redwood-evals/vectora/20260320/ (will paste run id when finished).
riya: quick test request: maya, please try qconfig with clip_threshold=0.02 and per_channel=false and post the sample answers.
maya: running now; if that fixes quality we'll push a qconfig patch and re-canary at smaller %, and add regression alert.
nora: two enterprise customers reported bad conversions in dashboards — @sam please prepare short RCA blurb and customer-safe summary for CS.
sam: on it, will draft. also adding a perf blurb for SRE. Should we add a regression alert in the Console?
maya: yes add an eval regression alert for currency/date tests. threshold: MAE > 5x baseline.
axel: infra note: observed 3x GPU memcpy spikes correlated with batch=8 at ~10:23 UTC on host a100-canary-3; attaching logs to the canary ticket.
riya: OK ownership/next steps: maya (repro & qconfig experiments), axel (driver/kernel diff + revert test), sam (customer comms + perf summary), nora (rollback + canary % decision), riya (eval runs + metric diffs). Update this thread with run ids and small diffs.
maya: update 2923456890: qconfig clip_threshold=0.02 per_channel=false reduces bad conversions; p50 back to ~230ms, p95 ~560ms. uploaded run_20260320_02 to s3.
nora: keep canary at 10% until we confirm stable metrics for 24h. Thanks team :clap:
